content:
GPU correctness passed without implementation repair. The single matched old/new/old diagnostic measured release→first token of **79.3 → 47.7 → 84.2 ms**. Adoption deltas were **-31.6 / -36.5 ms** against the two old controls; their repeat variation was **4.9 ms**. This is favorable preliminary direction for this handoff, not repeatable superiority or a comparison against demand. Readiness is excluded; no extra sweep or demand anchor ran.

All four arms passed every delivery gate. Each used the prior exact 2,048-token Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct prefix, BF16/TP1/block16, 640 GPU blocks (280 MiB), 448 MiB DRAM, 128 staging blocks, 750 ms privileged correct-target lead, native ARC threshold 2, request_order selection, soft retention off and owned_reclaimable staging. Each fresh server performed the identical 256 cold-source admission requests with GPU-only reset and six pressure requests. The target was fully ready in DRAM and absent from GPU at hint origin. The only generic config difference was wait_hint_native_adoption. Demand release never waited for hint acknowledgment. This is not deployable prediction.

The actual 56 MiB H2D transfer completed before publication. All 128 staged physical blocks became the native request prefix under the exact ordered keys. The worker used those same IDs with 2,048 computed tokens, one newly allocated suffix block and only 14 locally executed prompt tokens. Readiness read the actual CUDA block table (~516 bytes) and verified equality; its one synchronization is excluded from timing. Timed arms used symmetric host bookkeeping/prepare-attention observations without extra CUDA synchronization. Real generation matched every output token and ordered key across all 264 requests per arm (2,736 output tokens, including 128 resume and 512 background). All 1,056 requests completed with zero failures. KV contents were not independently bitwise dumped; real-GPU cancellation/failure injection and other layouts remain untested. The unchanged implementation retains the previous 174 extension +13 native passing CPU tests, including 30 adoption cases.

| Metric | Old staging 1 | Native adoption | Old staging 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Release→first token (ms) | 79.278 | 47.674 | 84.168 |
| Actual-submit TTFT (ms) | 78.475 | 46.765 | 83.325 |
| Worker attention prepared after release (ms) | 53.992 | 20.332 | 56.767 |
| Background TTFT (ms) | 30.242 | 31.196 | 30.077 |
| Background mean ITL (ms) | 15.644 | 15.648 | 15.685 |
| Background elapsed (ms) | 8024.618 | 8027.684 | 8045.472 |
| Background tokens/s | 63.804 | 63.779 | 63.638 |
| Request overlap (ms) | 2245.823 | 2212.991 | 2253.866 |


Background ITL uses 511 intervals between 512 tokens; throughput divides 512 by actual background elapsed seconds. Decode spans intended resume release in every arm. Native-minus-old background TTFT deltas were +0.954/+1.119 ms, mean ITL +0.004/-0.037 ms and elapsed +3.066/-17.788 ms. These few observations cannot establish background neutrality or a causal penalty.

In the timed adoption arm, the real H2D fence was -745.878 ms relative to demand, publication +17.341 ms, scheduler allocator adoption +18.232 ms, host execute entry +19.103 ms and worker attention preparation +20.332 ms. Scheduler acknowledgment is not worker-ready; both worker timestamps are host boundaries, not device-kernel/completion timestamps. DMA durations are separate and never added to overlapping runner time.

Each old arm copied 56 MiB GPU→GPU for installation; adoption copied zero prefix GPU→GPU bytes and used zero demand H2D. Staging was 56 MiB in every arm. Old splice held 112 MiB of staging+destination prefix copies simultaneously; adoption kept one 56 MiB prefix copy. This is pool occupancy inside the fixed 280 MiB pool, not a reduction of preallocated VRAM. Observed Torch allocated/reserved maxima were identical (3,493,384,704 /3,697,278,976 bytes). All sampled pool accounting was consistent and target allocation failures were zero. Staging reservation byte-time was 44.802 /42.888 /44.922 MiB·s. Sampled refcount peaks miss the transient duplicate; completed splice evidence establishes that overlap. Per arm, preparation+gap H2D was 7,516,192,768 bytes; D2H was 58,720,256 bytes during preparation. Gap H2D was 56 MiB and gap D2H zero. Full counters and every paired delta are in evidence/measurements.json.

The 32–36 ms delta includes allocation, async scheduler/worker round trips and observation overhead, not just copy-kernel cost. It does not establish removal of the entire prior 40–56 ms interval. Rich preservation/snapshot logging is enabled in all arms and branches emit different attribution volumes; both absolute latency and the path delta can be affected. Ownership/protection naturally changes: old staging stays reserved through destination fencing, while adoption becomes evictable native cache ownership. Retention/admission and intended gap traffic remain matched. See review-notes.md for alternatives and scope. Review was by the operational owner, with no independent reviewer under the no-child parent brief.

GPU strain was four model lifecycles totaling 295.5 s (~4.9 minutes) of driver wall time, including startup, preparation, generation, shutdown and CPU compression; GPU busy time was not measured. The requests locally executed 1,116,292 prompt tokens and generated 10,944 tokens. No separate tiny-tensor context, CUDA build, profiler, dependency download or extra arm ran. Device entry was an idle RTX 5080 with no compute application, after a fresh finite native-Windows benchmark_quiet grant. No other owner was interrupted. Post-run telemetry is retained.

No source/runtime code changed during this continuation. Full/delta/runtime patches were refreshed and reverse-apply checked; file bytes match the CPU-validated implementation already integrated on Mac. New hooks and reproduction tools stay task-local outside Git. No commit/push/PR. Runtime remains the recovered authoritative Python subset plus pinned wheel additions, not the exact historical Git tree. Pins/provenance: evidence/frozen.json; ../evidence/baseline.json and implementation-pins.json; ../../evidence/environment-freeze.txt, runtime-stage.json, recovered-runtime-files.json and runtime-overlay.json.

Evidence: evidence/measurements.json (machine-readable cases, exactness digests, all deltas and gates); evidence/*-detail.json (full attribution); results/*/raw.json.gz and server logs (lossless originals); results/*/compression.json (round-trip hashes); evidence/*.activity.json (mediated operation and empty-tree receipts). REPRODUCE.md has commands. Cleanup/retention is recorded in evidence/cleanup.json and evidence/storage-handback.json. Shared caches, reusable environment, recovery sources and old results are preserved.
